about: Accuracy regression suite (npm run eval:regression). Checks were written from answers graded correct in the 100-question accuracy review (Oct 2026) and from facts verified on official Barbadian sources. include = groups of accepted phrasings (one per group must appear); exclude = phrases that signal a known error. protected = the question was answered correctly before, so a failure is a regression. Update a check when the underlying fact changes (e.g. a new Minimum Wage Order).

cases.question: What jobs are available in Barbados right now?
cases.basis: Vacancies change daily; a good answer points to the Barbados Job Register on labour.gov.bb (Ministry of Labour / National Employment Bureau). Behaviour check only.

cases.question: What is the latest news in Barbados today?
cases.basis: No live news; answer should say so and point to news sources (GOV.BB News/GIS, local media). Stale headlines like the Trident ID item must not be presented as latest.

cases.question: Is there a storm or hurricane warning for Barbados?
cases.basis: Warnings are live; answer should direct to the Department of Emergency Management and Barbados Meteorological Services (Met Office). Hurricane season is 1 June to 30 November.

cases.question: Where can I find a tyre repair shop near me?
cases.basis: Directory-dependent; a useful answer names tyre/tire repair shops or services rather than only asking a clarifying question. Weak behaviour check only.

cases.question: Which bus or route taxi should I take to Bridgetown?
cases.basis: Transport Board buses, yellow minibuses and white ZR route taxis (maroon stripe) all serve Bridgetown; standard fare BBD$3.50; check the destination sign.

cases.question: How do I renew my Barbados passport?
cases.basis: Passports are handled by the Barbados Immigration Department (or missions abroad); appointments are booked online at immigration.gov.bb; applicants over 16 complete Form A. The 2022 'new passports from today, Monday, December 12' news must not be presented as current.

cases.question: Why is my electricity or water off, and when will it return?
cases.basis: Outages are live; answer should direct electricity issues to Barbados Light & Power (BL&P) and water issues to the Barbados Water Authority (BWA).

cases.question: What events are happening in Barbados this weekend?
cases.basis: Events change weekly; answer should point to a real events listing such as Visit Barbados events and festivals.

cases.question: Where can I find the best price for building materials?
cases.basis: Prices change; answer should name real suppliers (e.g. Carter & Co, Home Improvement & Hardware Supplies) and advise checking current prices. Invented businesses (S.A.M., B.D.M., K.M.M.) are errors.

cases.question: Where can I rent an affordable apartment in Christ Church?
cases.basis: Adulo Apartments (Rockley Hill, Christ Church) is a valid budget option; long-term rentals via real-estate listings. Best E Villas Prospect is in St. James, not Christ Church.

cases.question: Which doctors, clinics or pharmacies are open now?
cases.basis: Live open status is unknowable; answer should list pharmacies/clinics with listed hours (alpha.gov.bb find-an-open-pharmacy) and advise confirming. Behaviour check only.

cases.question: How do I apply for an NIS benefit or pension?
cases.basis: Benefits (sickness, maternity, old-age contributory/non-contributory pension, etc.) are claimed from the National Insurance and Social Security Service using its claim forms (nis.gov.bb online forms/NIS Portal) or at the Frank Walcott Building, Culloden Road, St. Michael; tel (246) 431-7400 / 467-4647.

cases.question: What scholarships or training programmes are available?
cases.basis: Includes government scholarships (National Development Scholarship, Barbados Scholarships/Exhibitions), Chevening etc., and training such as Job Start Plus (ages 16-24) and Barbados YouthADVANCE Corps.

cases.question: How do I register a business in Barbados?
cases.basis: Register with CAIPO (Business Barbados): Form 1 for a business name, fee BDS$104, online or by appointment; register within 14 days of starting if not trading under own surname.

cases.question: What are my rights as an employee, tenant or consumer?
cases.basis: Should give substance or pointers: employee rights (Employment Rights Act, Labour Department/Ministry of Labour), consumer rights (Consumer Protection Act, Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Fair Trading Commission). A bare clarifying question fails.

cases.question: Where can I pay a bill or a government fee online?
cases.basis: Government fees are paid online through EZPay+ (ezpay.gov.bb), by credit/Visa debit card or direct debit, 24/7.

cases.question: Where can I get vehicle repairs, parts or an inspection?
cases.basis: Repairs/parts from auto repair shops and parts dealers (e.g. SBA directory listings); vehicle inspections are done by the Barbados Licensing Authority (BLA) or its approved private garages.

cases.question: What are this week's supermarket specials?
cases.basis: Specials change weekly; answer should say it has no live specials and point to AskDealia (askdealia.gov.bb), the Government price-comparison service, or supermarkets directly.

cases.question: Who can repair or maintain my home, like a plumber or electrician?
cases.basis: Names plumbers/electricians from directories; only licensed electricians may submit inspection/alteration applications to the Government Electrical Engineering Department (GEED).

cases.question: How do I report a pothole or make a complaint?
cases.basis: Report potholes to the Ministry of Transport and Works (tel 536-0059, issue-report form, @mtwbarbados); vehicle damage claims via its Legal Unit. GEED/Chief Electrical Officer is irrelevant to roads.

cases.question: How do I get a birth certificate in Barbados?
cases.basis: Apply to the Registration Department (Supreme Court) online via EZPay+ or in person; $5 BBD per certified copy ($1 for 60+); ready in 5-7 business days.

cases.question: How do I apply for a Barbados driver's licence?
cases.basis: Through the Barbados Licensing Authority: apply with photos/proof of age and residence, pass the Regulations Test, get a Learner's Permit, pass the driving test, then pay for the licence ($50).

cases.question: How do I register a vehicle in Barbados?
cases.basis: Register at the Barbados Licensing Authority with customs declaration (C63), insurance certificate, weight and examiner's certificates, form LA 33; inspection at BLA or approved garage.

cases.question: How do I get a police certificate of character?
cases.basis: Forms from the Certificate of Character Office, Sugar Cane Mall, Roebuck Street, Bridgetown; submit police-taken fingerprints and passport copy; fee $20 BBD; valid six months.

cases.question: How do I apply for a Barbados ID card?
cases.basis: Apply to the Electoral and Boundaries Commission (Warrens Towers II, 535-4800) with original/certified birth certificate or Barbados passport (plus immigration status if not born in Barbados); citizens or residents permitted 6+ months.

cases.question: What government services can I use online on Alpha?
cases.basis: Alpha (alpha.gov.bb/services) offers online government services such as copies of birth/death/marriage certificates, notarisation, food business/restaurant/hairdresser licences, financial and disaster relief assistance. The exact list changes, so only a few stable examples are checked.

cases.question: How do I get a marriage licence in Barbados?
cases.basis: Both parties apply in person (by appointment) at the Ministry of Home Affairs and Information with original birth certificates and ID; the licence is valid for three months.

cases.question: How do I apply for a work permit in Barbados?
cases.basis: Work permits are issued by the Barbados Immigration Department; the prospective employer normally applies on the worker's behalf (short-term permits up to 11 months, long-term up to 3 years), booking an appointment via immigration.gov.bb.

cases.question: How do I register a death in Barbados?
cases.basis: A Notice of Death plus the doctor's Medical Certificate of (cause of) Death and the deceased's ID are lodged with the Registration Department (Supreme Court Complex, Whitepark Road, St. Michael) or district registrar, usually by the funeral director, within 5 days of death.

cases.question: Where is the Barbados Licensing Authority?
cases.basis: The BLA headquarters is at The Pine, St. Michael (with a branch at Holetown, St. James); tel. 536-0270, bla.gov.bb.

cases.question: How do I find a job through the National Employment Bureau?
cases.basis: Job seekers register with the National Employment Bureau (Ministry of Labour), which matches them to vacancies; vacancies change constantly so only the behaviour (register with the NEB / where to go) is checked.

cases.question: What does the Ministry of Labour do?
cases.basis: The Ministry of Labour promotes decent and productive work, employment and workforce development, harmonious industrial relations, labour legislation/rights at work, occupational safety and health, and elimination of child labour.

cases.question: How do I renew my driving permit?
cases.basis: Renewals are handled by the Barbados Licensing Authority; payment online via EZPay (one-year renewals) or at a Barbados Revenue Authority branch; drivers 75+ need a medical certificate.

cases.question: How do I apply for a tax identification number?
cases.basis: A TIN is obtained by registering with the Barbados Revenue Authority through its TAMIS portal (tamis.bra.gov.bb).

cases.question: Where can I get help as a small business owner?
cases.basis: Support bodies include the Barbados Small Business Association, Export Barbados (formerly BIDC), Enterprise Growth Fund / FundAccess and the small-business ministry; programmes change, so only that a real support body is named is checked, and the invented 'NEDC' is excluded.

cases.question: How much is the bus fare in Barbados?
cases.basis: The Transport Board adult fare is BBD $3.50, exact fare, no change given.

cases.question: Where is the Fairchild Street bus terminal?
cases.basis: The Fairchild Street Bus Terminal is on Fairchild Street in Bridgetown, near the Chamberlain Bridge/Careenage, and mainly serves south and east routes. Only Bridgetown/Fairchild Street are checked because street-level detail is worded too variably.

cases.question: How do I get from the airport to Bridgetown by bus?
cases.basis: Transport Board buses run from the airport along the south coast into Bridgetown's Fairchild Street Terminal for BBD $3.50 exact fare. Route 27 goes north to Speightstown and is wrong advice.

cases.question: What are Transport Board bus routes to Speightstown?
cases.basis: Route 1 (and variants) runs between Princess Alice Bus Terminal in Bridgetown and Speightstown Terminal along the west coast; Route 27 links Speightstown with the airport.

cases.question: What are ZR vans?
cases.basis: ZRs are privately owned route taxis/minivans (white with a maroon stripe) on fixed routes; fare is the same as Transport Board buses (BBD $3.50), so a $2 fare is outdated.

cases.question: Do Barbados buses run on Sundays?
cases.basis: Yes, buses run on Sundays and public holidays but on reduced schedules that vary by route.

cases.question: How do I get to Oistins by public transport?
cases.basis: Buses and ZRs to Oistins leave Bridgetown from the Fairchild Street Terminal and run along the south coast (Highway 7); fare BBD $3.50.

cases.question: Can I pay the bus fare with a card?
cases.basis: The Transport Board is rolling out cashless payments in phases; for now passengers pay the exact BBD $3.50 fare in cash.

cases.question: What time does the last bus leave Bridgetown?
cases.basis: Last departures vary by route and day and schedules change, so only behaviour is checked: say it depends on the route and point to Transport Board/Transit246 timetables.

cases.question: How do I get around Barbados without a car?
cases.basis: Options are Transport Board buses, privately operated yellow minibuses and ZR route taxis, and taxis.

cases.question: When did Barbados become independent?
cases.basis: Barbados became independent on 30 November 1966.

cases.question: When did Barbados become a republic?
cases.basis: Barbados became a parliamentary republic on 30 November 2021.

cases.question: Who is the President of Barbados?
cases.basis: Jeffrey Bostic has been President since 30 November 2025, succeeding Dame Sandra Mason (first President, 2021-2025).

cases.question: Who was Errol Barrow?
cases.basis: Errol Barrow (1920-1987), DLP leader, was Barbados's first Prime Minister and led it to independence on 30 November 1966; a National Hero, commemorated on Errol Barrow Day (21 January).

cases.question: Who are the national heroes of Barbados?
cases.basis: The eleven National Heroes: Bussa, Sarah Ann Gill, Samuel Jackman Prescod, Charles Duncan O'Neal, Clement Payne, Grantley Adams, Errol Barrow, Hugh Springer, Garfield Sobers, Frank Walcott and Rihanna (2021).

cases.question: What is Crop Over?
cases.basis: Crop Over is Barbados' biggest festival, celebrating the end of the sugar cane harvest (origins 1687, revived 1974); it runs from early July (about five to six weeks) to Grand Kadooment on the first Monday in August.

cases.question: What is the history of sugar in Barbados?
cases.basis: Sugar cane was introduced in the 1640s (from Dutch Brazil) and replaced tobacco and cotton; it built a plantation economy worked by enslaved Africans. Its history is shown at the Sir Frank Hutson Sugar Museum at Portvale.

cases.question: Why is Barbados called Little England?
cases.basis: Settled by the English in 1627 and under unbroken British rule for over 300 years, Barbados took on English-style governance, law, architecture and customs. That is why it is called Little England.

cases.question: What is the Barbados Garrison?
cases.basis: A historic British military complex next to Bridgetown (St Ann's Fort, barracks, the Savannah parade ground), once the largest in the British Caribbean. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison, inscribed in 2011.

cases.question: What is Bridgetown and its Garrison a UNESCO World Heritage Site for?
cases.basis: Inscribed in 2011 (criteria ii, iii, iv) as an outstanding example of British colonial architecture. The reasons are: the old town's 17th-century winding (serpentine) street layout, which shows an English approach to colonial town planning unlike the Spanish or Dutch grids; and the nearby Garrison, the military complex that protected the port and Atlantic trade.

cases.question: What is the story of Bussa's rebellion?
cases.basis: In April 1816 Bussa, an African-born enslaved man, led the largest slave revolt in Barbados' history. Nanny Grigg, an enslaved domestic woman, was one of its organisers. The revolt was crushed with hundreds of rebels killed, but it strengthened the abolition movement.

cases.question: What language do Barbadians speak?
cases.basis: English is the official language. Bajan, an English-based creole, is widely spoken informally.

cases.question: What is tuk band music?
cases.basis: Tuk (rukatuk) is Barbadian folk music that blends British military band music with African rhythms. It is played on a bass drum, snare (kettle) drum and penny whistle or flute (earlier a fiddle), sometimes with a triangle.

cases.question: What is the national dish of Barbados?
cases.basis: Cou-cou (cornmeal and okra) and flying fish.

cases.question: Who is Rihanna and where is she from?
cases.basis: Robyn Rihanna Fenty is a singer and entrepreneur (Fenty Beauty). She was born in St Michael, Barbados (raised on Westbury Road, Bridgetown) and was named a National Hero in 2021.

cases.question: What are Bajan fish cakes and where can I try them?
cases.basis: Deep-fried fritters of salted cod (saltfish) in a seasoned batter, eaten with pepper sauce or in salt bread as a 'bread and two'. They are sold by street vendors, rum shops, bakeries and fish fries (e.g. Oistins).

cases.question: What is cou-cou and flying fish?
cases.basis: The national dish of Barbados: cou-cou is cornmeal and okra stirred until firm, served with steamed or fried flying fish and a spicy gravy.

cases.question: Where is the Oistins Friday fish fry?
cases.basis: At Oistins Bay Garden in Oistins, a fishing town in Christ Church on the south coast, on Friday nights.

cases.question: What is a Bajan cutter?
cases.basis: A sandwich made on a Bajan salt bread roll, filled with flying fish, fish cakes, ham, cheese or egg, often with pepper sauce.

cases.question: What drinks is Barbados known for?
cases.basis: Rum (Barbados is the birthplace of rum; Mount Gay dates to 1703), rum punch, Banks beer, mauby, sorrel, falernum and local juices.

cases.question: Where can I find restaurants on the west coast?
cases.basis: Behaviour check only, because restaurant listings change. The west coast covers St James and St Peter (Holetown, Paynes Bay, Sunset Crest, Speightstown). Champers is in Hastings on the south coast and must not appear as a west coast restaurant.

cases.question: What is pudding and souse?
cases.basis: A Saturday Bajan dish. Pudding is spiced, grated sweet potato steamed in a pig-intestine casing. Souse is pork (head, trotters) pickled in lime juice with onion, cucumber and pepper.

cases.question: Where can I eat local food in Bridgetown?
cases.basis: Behaviour check, because eateries change. Local Bajan lunch spots in and next to Bridgetown include Mustor's Restaurant (McGregor Street), stalls around Cheapside Market, the Pelican Village area and the Baxter's Road vendors. Chefette is a local chain. The Tides is a Holetown fine-dining restaurant, not a Bridgetown option, and Oistins is in Christ Church.

cases.question: Is Mount Gay rum from Barbados?
cases.basis: Yes. Mount Gay is made in Barbados (St Lucy) and is documented back to 1703, making it the world's oldest commercial rum brand.

cases.question: What dining experiences does Visit Barbados recommend?
cases.basis: Behaviour check. Visit Barbados recommends Oistins fish fry, Dine With A Bajan, Lickrish Food Tours, fine dining, rum shops, street food and casual local spots such as Mustor's and Cutters.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Barbados as a visitor?
cases.basis: A valid passport, a return or onward ticket, an address in Barbados, proof of funds, a parental letter for unaccompanied minors and a visa only if your nationality needs one. Visitors also fill in the online immigration/customs form (ED card) before arrival.

cases.question: What currency is used in Barbados?
cases.basis: The Barbados dollar (BBD), the only legal tender, is pegged to the US dollar at BBD$2 = US$1. 1.98 is only a bank buying rate.

cases.question: Which beaches are best on the south and west coasts?
cases.basis: South coast: Accra/Rockley, Dover, Miami (Enterprise) Beach, Sandy Beach (Worthing), Welches, Silver Sands, plus Carlisle Bay/Brownes on the south-west. West coast (St James and St Peter): Paynes Bay, Mullins, Gibbes, Sandy Lane, Holetown, Heywoods, Batts Rock, Brighton. Crane Beach is on the south-east coast (St Philip), not the west.

cases.question: What can I do in Bridgetown in one day?
cases.basis: A day in Bridgetown can take in the UNESCO historic city and Garrison, Parliament Buildings and National Heroes Square, the Careenage and Chamberlain Bridge, Nidhe Israel Synagogue, the Barbados Museum, shopping on Broad Street, Cheapside Market and Pelican Village, and a swim at Carlisle Bay.

cases.question: What is the Barbados Welcome Stamp?
cases.basis: A 12-month visa launched in 2020 that lets location-independent remote workers and their families live in Barbados. You apply online and can renew.

cases.question: When is the best time to visit Barbados?
cases.basis: Dry season (December to May) is generally best; wet/hurricane season June to November, but the island is warm and visitable year-round.

cases.question: Is tap water safe to drink in Barbados?
cases.basis: Yes: Barbados tap water (supplied by the Barbados Water Authority, filtered through coral limestone) is safe to drink.

cases.question: What is Harrison's Cave?
cases.basis: A limestone show cave in the central uplands (St. Thomas) with stalactites/stalagmites, streams and pools, toured by tram (plus eco-adventure tours); features the Great Hall.

cases.question: Where can I see green monkeys in Barbados?
cases.basis: Barbados Wildlife Reserve (St. Peter, best around the 2pm feeding) and Welchman Hall Gully (St. Thomas) are the main places to see green monkeys.

cases.question: What should I know about driving in Barbados?
cases.basis: Driving is on the left; visitors need a temporary driving permit (BDS$10 under 2 months, $100 up to a year) from the Licensing Authority or car hire firms; speed limits 80 km/h highways, 60 km/h elsewhere, 40 km/h in town; hands-free phone use only.

cases.question: How do I get a TAMIS tax account?
cases.basis: Register online at tamis.bra.gov.bb to obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN); BRA support at 535-ETAX (535-3829) or bramail@bra.gov.bb.

cases.question: What is the minimum wage in Barbados?
cases.basis: National minimum wage is BDS$10.71 per hour from 21 January 2026 (2% increase from $10.50); security guards have a separate sectoral rate. Update this check if a new Minimum Wage Order is made.

cases.question: How do I apply for a job in the public service?
cases.basis: Public service jobs are handled by the Ministry of the Public Service (People Resourcing and Compliance Directorate); vacancies are posted at mps.gov.bb, contact (246) 535-4500. The old 467-4500 number is outdated.

cases.question: What should I do to prepare for a hurricane?
cases.basis: StormReady checklist: secure home/shutters, store 3 gallons of water per person for 3 days, non-perishable food, documents in waterproof bag, cash, charged devices and radio for DEM updates, know nearest shelter.

cases.question: How do I contact the Barbados Water Authority?
cases.basis: BWA Customer Service (246) 434-4292 (434-4BWA), daily 8:30am-midnight; PBX (246) 434-4200; customercare@bwa.gov.bb; office at Pine Commercial Estate, St. Michael. (The 426-3990 number in the earlier answer could not be verified.)

cases.question: Where can I renew a vehicle licence or pay road tax?
cases.basis: Motor vehicle licence (road tax) is paid to the Barbados Revenue Authority, at any BRA branch or online (BRA/EZPay), not at the Licensing Authority.

cases.question: What public holidays does Barbados have?
cases.basis: 12 holidays: New Year's Day, Errol Barrow Day (21 Jan), Good Friday, Easter Monday, National Heroes' Day (28 Apr), Labour Day (1 May), Whit Monday, Emancipation Day (1 Aug), Kadooment Day (1st Mon Aug), Independence Day (30 Nov), Christmas Day, Boxing Day.

cases.question: How do I find a polyclinic near me?
cases.basis: Government polyclinics include Branford Taitt (Black Rock), Maurice Byer (St. Peter), Winston Scott (Bridgetown), Eunice Gibson (Warrens), David Thompson (St. John), Frederick Miller/Glebe (St. George), Randal Phillips (Oistins), Edgar Cochrane (Wildey), St. Philip (Six Roads).

cases.question: How do I sign up for the National Insurance Scheme?
cases.basis: Register with the National Insurance Department, Frank Walcott Building, Culloden Road, St. Michael (tel. 431-7400 / 467-4NIS), bringing national ID; employees are usually registered via their employer.

cases.question: Where can I learn about Barbados Revenue Authority services?
cases.basis: The BRA website bra.gov.bb (Popular Topics, Apply, Help, Service Charter pages) describes its services.

cases.question: What exactly are Bajan fish cakes, and how are they prepared?
cases.basis: Bajan fish cakes are fritters of salted cod (desalted by boiling, flaked) mixed with flour, baking powder, herbs, onion and hot pepper, deep-fried; often eaten in salt bread ('bread and two') with Marie Rose or pepper sauce.

cases.question: What is the difference between pudding and souse and cou-cou and flying fish?
cases.basis: Pudding and souse: pickled pork (lime, cucumber, onion, pepper) with steamed spiced sweet-potato pudding, a Saturday tradition. Cou-cou and flying fish: cornmeal-and-okra cou-cou with (usually steamed) flying fish in sauce, the national dish.

cases.question: How can I renew my Barbados driver's licence, and what documents do I need?
cases.basis: Renew by paying the fee at any BRA branch or online via EZPay, presenting the expiring licence and ID; drivers 75+ need a medical certificate every 2 years, 85+ every year; licence collected from the Barbados Licensing Authority.

cases.question: Which bus should I take from Bridgetown to Bathsheba, and where do I board it?
cases.basis: Take the Transport Board's Bathsheba bus (route 6, roughly hourly, about 1 hour) from the Fairchild Street Terminal in Bridgetown; route 1E runs from Speightstown, not Bridgetown. Diversions are temporary and are not checked.

cases.question: What are the steps and costs for registering a small business in Barbados?
cases.basis: Register a business name with CAIPO by filing Form 1 (online or in person); filing fee BDS$104.

cases.question: Where can I find a reasonably priced apartment to rent in St. Philip?
cases.basis: No stable facts (listings and prices change constantly); a good answer admits it has no live listings and points to real estate/rental agencies, classifieds or online marketplaces.

cases.question: Are there any current vacancies for electricians in Barbados?
cases.basis: Vacancies change daily; a good answer points to the Barbados Job Register / Ministry of Labour (National Employment Bureau) rather than inventing openings.

cases.question: What are three historical places in Bridgetown that a visitor can explore on foot?
cases.basis: Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison (UNESCO) sites include the Parliament Buildings, Nidhe Israel Synagogue, St. Michael's Cathedral, Blackwoods Screw Dock, the Garrison Savannah, Barbados Museum and George Washington House.

cases.question: Can I legally operate a food vending business from a vehicle in Barbados, and which approvals are required?
cases.basis: Yes, with a Food Business Licence (covers food sold from vehicles); the vehicle is inspected by an Environmental Health Officer and the licence must be displayed.

cases.question: Where can I buy a second-hand refrigerator in Barbados for under BDS$500?
cases.basis: No stable facts (stock and prices change); a good answer admits it cannot confirm stockists and points to online marketplaces/classifieds or second-hand/used-appliance sellers.
